en.title: Regional differences
en.summary: Accents, attitudes and habits that differ by region, and how to avoid stereotypes.

paragraphs: Regions differ in speech, food, prices and attitudes. This lesson compares them and teaches you to talk about differences without sounding unfair.

People often say that there is a north-south divide in England. House prices, salaries and the cost of living are generally higher in the south, particularly in and around London. People in the north are said to be more talkative with strangers. These are generalisations, and there are many exceptions. Two colleagues compare regions.

lines.speaker: Ian
lines.text: People in the north tend to be more talkative with strangers.

lines.speaker: Mary
lines.text: That is a stereotype, but there is some truth in it.

lines.speaker: Ian
lines.text: And the south is more expensive.

lines.speaker: Mary
lines.text: Yes, house prices in London are much higher than in Wales.

lines.speaker: Ian
lines.text: Do you think the north will catch up?

lines.speaker: Mary
lines.text: Some northern cities, such as Manchester, have grown quickly, so the gap is getting smaller.

lines.speaker: Ian
lines.text: That's interesting. I'd like to see it for myself.

paragraphs: **1. Much, far and a bit modify comparatives.** They show how big the difference is. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives.

blocks.html:
FormExample
much highermuch higher than in Wales
a bit cheapera bit cheaper than London
far more expensivefar more expensive than the north
slightly lowerslightly lower than average

paragraphs: **2. Tend to and generally soften generalisations.** They avoid saying that all people behave the same way. See Introduction to Grammar: Verbs and verb phrases.

blocks.html:
FormExample
tend to + verbPeople tend to be friendly.
generallyPrices are generally higher.
on the wholeOn the whole, it is cheaper.
There are exceptions.but there are many exceptions

items: A stereotype is a fixed idea about a group.
There is a north-south divide in England in income and accent.
In the United States, regions have different political traditions.
Catch up means to reach the same level.

paragraphs: Regional pride is strong, and it is shown in sports teams, food and local dialects. Friendly rivalry between regions is common, and it is usually expressed as humour rather than hostility.
